intro: Type a linear equation in x, such as 3x + 5 = 20 or 2(x − 1) = x + 4, and get the value of x with each step of the working. If the answer is not a whole number, it is shown as an exact fraction.

formula.label: Expanding a bracket
formula.note: Multiply every term inside by the number outside.

formula.label: Basic form
formula.expr: ax + b = c  →  x = (c − b) ÷ a

formula.label: x on both sides
formula.expr: ax + b = cx + d  →  (a − c)x = d − b  →  x = (d − b) ÷ (a − c)

howItWorks: An equation is like a balance: whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other. The solver first expands any brackets, so 2(x − 1) becomes 2x − 2. Then it moves all the x terms to one side and all the plain numbers to the other, and finally divides by the number in front of x.

Sometimes the x terms cancel out completely. If you are left with something false, like 1 = 2, the equation has no solution. If you are left with something always true, like 2 = 2, then every number is a solution. The solver tells you which case you have.
When x does not come out as a whole number, you see it as a fraction in lowest terms, such as x = 7/2, so nothing is lost to rounding.

example.title: Brackets and x on both sides

mistakes.title: Only multiplying the first term in a bracket
mistakes.text: 2(x − 1) is 2x − 2, not 2x − 1. The number outside multiplies every term inside.

mistakes.title: Forgetting to change the sign
mistakes.text: When you move a term across the equals sign, you do the opposite operation. From 3x + 5 = 20, take 5 from both sides to get 3x = 15, not 3x = 25.

mistakes.title: Dividing only part of a side
mistakes.text: From 3x + 6 = 12 you cannot jump to x + 6 = 4. Take away 6 first to get 3x = 6, then divide by 3 to get x = 2.

mistakes.title: Dropping a minus sign in front of a bracket
mistakes.text: A minus in front of a bracket changes every sign inside: −(x − 3) = −x + 3, not −x − 3.

faqs.a: It means no value of x makes both sides equal. For x + 1 = x + 2, taking x from both sides leaves 1 = 2, which is never true.

faqs.q: What does every number is a solution mean?
faqs.a: It means the two sides are the same expression written differently. 2x + 2 = 2(x + 1) is true for any x, because 2(x + 1) expands to 2x + 2.

faqs.q: How do I type a fraction of x?
faqs.a: Use a slash, for example x/3 + 2 = 5. Taking 2 from both sides gives x/3 = 3, and multiplying by 3 gives x = 9.

faqs.q: How can I check my answer?
faqs.a: Put your value of x back into both sides of the original equation. If both sides give the same number, the answer is right.

faqs.q: Can it solve equations with x²?
faqs.a: No. This solver is for linear equations, where x is never raised to a power. For equations like x² − 5x + 6 = 0, use a quadratic solver.
